title: Data Types: Numbers, Characters, Strings, Booleans, and Aggregates
description: How integers, floats, characters, strings, booleans, arrays, objects, and structures compare across the three languages.
objectives: Compare numeric type systems (fixed-size vs. arbitrary precision)

content.heading: Python
content.body: int has arbitrary precision (no overflow, grows as needed); float is a 64-bit double. bool is a true boolean subtype of int. str is an immutable sequence of Unicode code points, with no separate 'character' type — a single character is just a length-1 string. Aggregates: list (mutable, dynamic array), and full objects via classes.

content.heading: Java
content.body: Integers are fixed-size (byte/short/int/long), with silent wraparound on overflow (no exception). boolean is a true, distinct primitive type. char is a 16-bit Unicode code unit; String is an immutable object (not a primitive). Aggregates: fixed-size arrays, and rich objects via classes with the full Collections Framework on top.

content.heading: C
content.body: Integers are fixed-size (char/short/int/long), platform- and compiler-dependent in exact size, with signed overflow being undefined behavior (unsigned overflow wraps, defined). There is no built-in boolean type in classic C (int is used, or _Bool/stdbool.h's bool since C99). A string is just a char array ending in '\0' — there's no distinct string type. Aggregates: fixed-size arrays and structs (struct), with no built-in dynamic collection types at all.

content.heading: Key Differences
content.body: Python's int never overflows; Java's and C's fixed-size integers can (Java wraps silently; C's signed overflow is undefined behavior, arguably worse). Only Java has a true, enforced boolean type among the three (C's pre-C99 lack of one, and its weak int-as-boolean convention, is a notable gap). Strings: Python's str and Java's String are genuine, safe, immutable types; C strings are just conventionally-terminated char arrays with no built-in safety.

content.heading: When It Matters
content.body: Porting numeric code from Python to Java or C requires actively considering overflow, something Python code never has to think about. Porting string-processing code to C requires manually managing buffer sizes and null termination, responsibilities neither Python nor Java places on the programmer.

keyPoints: Python's int has arbitrary precision; Java's and C's integers are fixed-size and can overflow
Only Java has a genuinely built-in, enforced boolean type among the three
C strings are raw char arrays with a null terminator; Python's str and Java's String are safe, dedicated types
